claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for child benefit. 

Let me start by asking: Do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have a son, Alex, who's 18 and still lives at home with me. I'm wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for him now that he's turned 18?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand his current situation.

Is Alex currently in full-time approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. I need to understand a bit more about when Alex started this course and when he turned 18.

What date did Alex turn 18?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 18 in September this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And when did Alex start his current A-level course at college?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He started his A-levels in September last year, so he's in his second year now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Just to clarify - did Alex turn 18 before or after the start of the current academic year in September? In other words, did he turn 18 before or after early September 2024 when the new term would have started?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 18 after the term started - so it was later in September, after college had already gone back.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Now I need to ask a few more questions about your personal circumstances.

Are you currently responsible for Alex - meaning do you live with him and are you responsible for his upbringing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives at home with me and I look after him - I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's helpful. Let me ask: Is Alex your own child, or is he someone else's child that you're looking after?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's my own child, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

Are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just one more important question:

Does anyone else currently claim Child Benefit for Alex, or are you the only person claiming (or intending to claim) for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming for him. I'm the only one.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just ask one final question to complete my assessment:

When does Alex's A-level course end? Is it scheduled to finish before or after he turns 20?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's a two-year course, so it'll finish next summer when he's 19 - well before he turns 20.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Even though Alex is 18, you can continue to claim Child Benefit for him because:

- He is under 20 years old
- He is in approved full-time education (his A-levels)
- He lives with you and you're responsible for him
- You live in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex until his A-level course finishes next summer (as long as he remains in approved education and is under 20). 

If you haven't already been claiming Child Benefit for Alex, you can make a claim. If you've been claiming all along, you can continue to do so while he completes his A-levels.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

However, if your child is 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training. In this case: (1) Alex is 18 years old, which is under 20; (2) He is in full-time approved education (A-levels at college); (3) He started his A-level course in September last year before turning 18; (4) He turned 18 after the current academic year started (later in September after term began); (5) You are responsible for Alex - he is your own child, lives with you, and you look after him; (6) You live in the UK; (7) Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex; (8) His course will finish next summer when he's 19, which is before he turns 20. Based on these facts, Alex meets the criteria for Child Benefit as he is under 20 and in approved education. Therefore, you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.
